name: Pramiracetam
summary: Pramiracetam is a racetam medicine thought to help learning and memory; it is not FDA-approved but is prescribed in some European countries for cognitive decline.
description: Pramiracetam is a fat-soluble medicine from the racetam family, developed in the late 1970s. It is thought to work mainly by helping brain cells take up choline, which increases the production of acetylcholine, a brain chemical involved in memory, in the hippocampus (a memory area of the brain). This is believed to explain its effects on learning and memory. Pramiracetam is not FDA-approved in the United States, but it is prescribed in some European countries for cognitive decline, dementia and recovery from brain injury.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Pramiracetam is a fat-soluble racetam derivative developed in the late 1970s. It is thought to work primarily by enhancing high-affinity choline uptake, thereby increasing acetylcholine synthesis and availability in the hippocampus. This mechanism is believed to underlie its effects on learning and memory. Pramiracetam is not FDA-approved in the United States but is prescribed in some European countries for cognitive decline, dementia, and brain injury recovery.
